researchUpdates.title: Carbonate-rich coffee husk ash as an alternative potassium source for metakaolin-based geopolymers
researchUpdates.journal: Journal of the Australian Ceramic Society
researchUpdates.authors: João Claudio Bassan de Moraes, Pamela Rodrigues Passos Severino, Rodolfo Belasco and Thiago Costa Ferreira Gomes
researchUpdates.summary: A metakaolin study compares KOH, potassium carbonate and laboratory-produced coffee husk ash as potassium sources, using calcium hydroxide to convert soluble carbonate species and restore alkalinity in the ash- and carbonate-based systems.
highlights: Coffee husk ash alone did not harden adequately under the selected low-calcium conditions; pairing it with calcium hydroxide changed the carbonate chemistry and enabled a testable geopolymer matrix.

The result depends on ash produced by a defined drying, two-stage calcination and milling route, followed by three days of sealed 60 °C curing; it is not evidence that raw or differently burned coffee waste will behave similarly.
researchUpdates.access: The primary Springer article, methods, author information and version history were reviewed. Five potassium-source systems were compared at fixed K₂O/metakaolin and water/binder ratios; only three hardened sufficiently for physical and compressive testing, with three cubes per condition. The laboratory ash came from one coffee-husk source and controlled calcination. Compression was measured after the stated thermal cure; no ambient-cured, tensile, flexural, shear, durability, leaching, scale-up or life-cycle result is inferred.
researchUpdates.summaryBasis: Primary Springer publisher page, full article text, methods, author information and version history; no abstract text, publisher highlights, figures, tables or full-paper passages were reproduced

journalArticle.title: Biomass ash is an activator-chemistry problem
journalArticle.summary: Coffee husk ash can supply potassium, but its carbonate form and processing history determine whether that potassium actually creates a sufficiently alkaline geopolymerization environment.
paragraphs: The useful idea is not simply to replace commercial KOH with ash by mass. The study first treats the ash as a chemically distinct potassium source: carbonate-rich, hygroscopic and less effective at dissolving metakaolin without a calcium-assisted causticization step.

For formulation records, preserve the biomass source, combustion schedule, milling, soluble fraction, potassium and carbonate content, calcium dose, K/Ca ratio, water definition and curing history. Those variables are part of the activator identity, not incidental preparation notes.
